title: The Path of Purification (Visuddhimagga)
author: Bhadantacariya Buddhaghosa
year: 5th century CE; translation 1956; BPS online ed. 2011
edition_cited: Buddhist Publication Society, Kandy, revised third online edition, 2011 (PDF text via archive.org)
locator_hints: Ch. IV (earth kasina): making the disk, gazing with eyes 'open moderately', apprehending 'a hundred times, a thousand times' until the learning sign arises; '[The Counterpart Sign]' (file line c. 11116-11160); guarding and extending the sign
Ch. V (remaining kasinas): water, fire (line c. 13758), air, colours, '[The Light Kasina]' V.21-23 (line 13878), limited space; V.36 on what the light kasina is a basis for
Ch. VIII, mindfulness of breathing: how the sign appears differently to different people (star, cluster of gems, cotton...; file line c. 20860-20880) and that it is born of perception
Ch. IV.55 ff.: perception of light as a remedy for torpor (line c. 11572)
Ch. XIII: divine eye and extending light (line c. 28115)
Ch. XX.105-130: the ten imperfections of insight beginning with illumination (obhasa), and how the skilful meditator treats it (file lines c. 44446-44720)
summary: The classical Theravada manual. Chapter IV gives the earth-kasina procedure in full: construction of the disk, distance and seat, gazing with eyes moderately open, alternately opening and closing them and adverting 'a hundred times, a thousand times' until the learning sign is seen with eyes shut as with eyes open; then leaving the place, developing the sign until the purified counterpart sign 'breaks out', and guarding and extending it. Chapter V treats fire, light (a circle of sun or lamp light on a wall; counterpart 'a compact bright cluster of lights'), colour and space kasinas. Chapter VIII lists how the breath sign appears to different meditators (star, gems, pearls, cotton, smoke, moon or sun disk) and attributes the variety to perception. Chapter XX treats illumination arising in early insight as the first of ten imperfections and prescribes seeing it as impermanent and not the path.
why_relevant: Foundational step-by-step instructions for turning a gazed-at object into a light seen with closed eyes, descriptions of the breath sign, and the tradition's own warning about insight-light.
